claims.statement: `GET /accounts/holdings` paginates positions, not accounts or holdings rows: `PositionRepository.get_by_user` counts `PositionModel` rows joined to the user's `AccountModel` rows and pages them with `order_by(PositionModel.id)`, so the response `total` is a position count and one account can contribute several items whose rows may be split across page boundaries because the service only ever regroups the fetched page.

`PositionService.get_user_holdings(user_id, offset, limit, display_currency)` buckets the repository's page by `account_id`, resolves each distinct account once through `AccountService.get_account` (not once per position), converts each position via `_calculate_holdings(account, account_positions, display_currency)`, and then layers account context onto the already-converted rows with `UserHoldingRead(**holding.model_dump(), account_id=account.id, account_name=account.name)`, returning the rows in account-first-appearance order together with the position count.

`PositionService.get_account_holdings` computes `total_value` and `total_profit_loss` over every position of the account (an unlimited `get_by_account` call) through `_calculate_holdings` plus `_account_performance`, while returning only one paginated page of `items`; the response carries `profit_loss_basis`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash` (already folded into `total_value`), `broker_value`/`broker_value_at`, `unpriced_positions` and `pricing_incomplete` alongside the paginated envelope and account identity.

`HoldingRead` carries three currency readings of the same position — native `unconverted_total_value`/`unconverted_profit_loss` in `security_currency`, account-currency `total_value`/`profit_loss`/`converted_average_cost`/`converted_latest_price` in `currency`, and display-currency `display_total_value`/`display_currency` — plus `latest_price`/`price_date`/`updated_at`; `UserHoldingRead` adds `account_id`/`account_name`; `AccountHoldingsRead` extends `PaginatedResponse[HoldingRead]` with account identity, totals, `profit_loss_basis`, `net_deposits`, `free_cash`, `broker_value`/`broker_value_at`, `currency`, `unpriced_positions` and `pricing_incomplete`; `AccountHoldingRead` carries `display_total_value`/`display_currency` next to its native value.

Authorization differs per holdings endpoint: `GET /accounts/holdings` is scoped implicitly by the repository's join on `AccountModel.user_id`, whereas `GET /accounts/{account_id}/holdings` and `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` look the account up and call `authorization_api.check_entity_owned_by_user`, which raises 404 for a missing or unowned account, before delegating to `PositionService`.

`_calculate_holdings` catches `SecurityNotFoundError` per position, logs "Security not found for position ...", increments the returned `unpriced_positions` count and continues, so the position produces no row while `total` still counts it; the response surfaces `unpriced_positions`/`pricing_incomplete` instead of hiding that the page returned fewer rows than it counted.

`PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` fills the repository's `AccountHoldingRead` placeholder rows (`total_value=0.0`, `currency=""`, `display_total_value=0.0`, `display_currency=""`) with `quantity × latest close` in the security currency, a `display_total_value` converted into `display_currency` (defaulting to each account's currency), `account_total_value` from `get_total_for_account` and `account_percentage` only when the account total is positive, and returns an ambiguous `([], 0)` when the security is unknown — behaviour the source marks with a TODO.

The `/holdings` load reads the query-string filter ids and issues three concurrent SSR reads — `getPreferences`, `getPortfolios` and `getAccounts` — under `Promise.allSettled`: a single rejection only leaves that slot at its fallback (`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig(null)`, `normalizeHoldingsGroupMode(null)`, `null` waves or an empty list), while a rejected result whose reason is an `ApiError` with status 401 clears the auth cookie and throws a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true` which the surrounding `catch` re-throws. The load returns `holdings_table_config`, `group_mode`, `elliott_waves`, `portfolios`, `accounts`, `portfolio_id` and `account_id`, and it never awaits or returns holdings rows.

SSR requests pass the `auth_token` cookie explicitly as a Bearer override because `ApiClient.get` only sets `Authorization: Bearer` when a token override is supplied (it always sets `credentials: 'include'`); the `/` and `/accounts/[id]` loads map a 401 to `deleteAuthCookie` plus a 303 redirect to `/auth/login?clear_session=true`, other `ApiError` statuses to Kit errors and anything else to a 500, and the `/holdings` load maps a 401 from any of its three SSR reads the same way, while its post-navigation 401 is routed through `redirectOn401`, which `goto`s `/auth/login?clear_session=true` without deleting the httpOnly cookie client-side (`hooks.server.ts` clears it when the login page resolves).

`/holdings` builds its header totals from the accounts' server totals, not from `service.rows`: the page derives `filteredAccounts` from the filter variant and has `service.loadAccountTotals` fetch their `GET /accounts/{id}/totals`, then buckets the cached `AccountTotals` by `account.currency` through `aggregateAccountTotals`, which sums `value` (cash included) and `profit_loss`, uses `sum(profit_loss)/sum(net_deposits)` when every account in the bucket reports the `net_deposits` basis and otherwise falls back to `sum(value − profit_loss)` labelled "mixed basis", and returns `returnPercent = null` for a zero denominator — values are never summed across currency buckets.

`groupHoldings` in `stock` mode (and its legacy `company` alias) keys strictly on `security_id`, keeps first-appearance ordering, sums `quantity`/`total_value`/`display_total_value`/`unconverted_total_value` and null-preserving P/L, computes quantity-weighted `average_cost` and `converted_average_cost`, dedupes `account_names` and counts distinct accounts; when the grouped rows span more than one account currency it instead sums `display_total_value` into `total_value`, labels the group with the first row's `display_currency` and forces `profit_loss` to `null`, because per-row P/L is never converted.

The `/holdings` page owns its `HoldingsService` instance instead of reading a layout context: it constructs the service, seeds the group mode with `setGroupBy(data.group_mode)`, re-applies the URL filter from `data.portfolio_id` / `data.account_id` in one `$effect`, triggers `service.load()` from a second single `$effect`, and drives the per-account totals wave from a third `$effect` that maps the derived `filteredAccounts` to ids and calls `loadAccountTotals` inside `untrack`; toggling grouping and changing the portfolio/account filter are therefore pure client-side derivations that never refetch holdings, and `getHoldingsService` remains the context/custom-fetch accessor for other callers.

`HoldingsService.load()` is the sole implementation of the collect-every-page contract: it loops `getUserHoldings(offset, PAGE_SIZE, token)` sequentially with `PAGE_SIZE = 50` and the `MAX_PAGES = 100` stale-total cap, breaks early on an empty page, stores the collected rows through the `rows` setter into `allRows`, then makes one batched `getValuationsBatch` read for the distinct security ids in its own nested `try/catch` that degrades to an empty map, toggles `isLoading` around the whole loop, never throws (it stores the message in `errorMessage`, keeps the previously loaded rows, and returns the caught error or `null`), and clears the error on the next success.

`holdings-table.svelte` stays presentational: it derives a normalized `HoldingsTableConfig` from the `tableConfig` prop, keeps a local copy so a column drag gives immediate feedback, and emits the final clamped config once at pointer-up via `onConfigChange`, while the `/holdings` page owns persistence and pushes write failures into a `holdings-error` alert without reverting the optimistic UI change.

`holdings_table` and `holdings_group` are persisted one top-level key at a time (`patchPreferences({ holdings_table: config })` / `patchPreferences({ holdings_group: mode })`) through an injected structural prefs service instead of the module singleton, matching the backend's top-level JSONB `||` merge so a concurrent write to a different preference key cannot be dropped (nested values of the same key remain last-write-wins).

`normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` guarantees a usable config from any stored shape: non-object/missing input yields defaults, unknown and retired column ids (including `average_cost`, `percent_of_total` and `profit_loss_percent`) are dropped from `widths` and `visible`, widths are clamped by `clampColumnWidth` (non-finite falls back to the default), surviving `visible` ids are re-ordered to canonical `HOLDINGS_TABLE_COLUMN_IDS` order with the sticky column force-included, an empty or fully invalid `visible` list falls back to all columns, and the returned object never aliases the defaults.

`HOLDINGS_TABLE_STICKY_COLUMN_ID` (`security_symbol`) can never be hidden: `toggleColumnVisibility` returns the same config object unchanged for it, the display-settings menu item is `disabled`, and the table renders its data cell and its skeleton cells with the sticky position classes when the column id matches the constant, while `normalizeHoldingsTableConfig` re-adds it to any stored `visible` list.

`normalizeHoldingsGroupMode` normalizes the persisted `holdings_group` value to `'stock'` only for `'stock'` and the legacy `'company'`, and to `'none'` for every other value (including `'STOCK'`, numbers, objects and `null`), so a stored legacy mode still renders grouped while the next save writes `'stock'`.

`AccountClient.getAccountHoldings(id, token)` sends no `offset`/`limit`, so `/accounts/[id]` receives the backend defaults (offset 0, limit 50 for `PaginationParams`) while `AccountHoldingsRead.total` and the header totals cover every position of the account, meaning accounts with more than 50 positions render truncated rows next to complete totals.

The accounts dashboard `/` reads only the account list (`GET /accounts/`, ordered by account name) in its server load and defers each row's value to a client-side `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` call that `PositionService.get_total_for_account` resolves by pricing the account's positions, converting into the account currency and returning `AccountTotals` (`cost`/`value`/`cash`/`profit_loss` as `Money` plus `basis`, `net_deposits`, `unpriced_positions` and `pricing_incomplete`); the per-item state caches the totals and the lazily-expanded holdings page per account and invalidates both together when a sync finishes or a CSV import succeeds, and expanding a row renders the inline holdings list from that cached page.

`/accounts/[id]` renders its header from `AccountHoldingsRead` through `TotalProfitLossButtons` (with `costBasis` taken from `net_deposits` and the basis label from `profit_loss_basis`, plus the `pricing_incomplete` warning) and its body through the separate presentational `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte`, which takes `holdings` and `totalAccountValue`, has no column configuration or grouping, shows native- and account-currency values side by side when they differ, annotates each row with its share of the account total, and is mounted only when `data.holdings.items.length > 0`.

The holdings read path's test suites follow the repository's mocking contract: the frontend suites mock every API client and framework module that performs network or browser work (`$lib/api/accountService`, `$lib/api/accountClient`, `$lib/api/marketService`, `$lib/api/userPreferencesService`, `$lib/api/valuationClient`, `$app/paths`, `$app/navigation`) and never call the backend, so numeric holdings math is asserted by the backend suites; they pin the preference-and-metadata-only load and its paging absence, the `HoldingsService` paging loop, stale-total guards and batched valuations, the `loadAccountTotals` cache and failure handling, per-currency header bucketing from the account totals, grouping toggles, the `redirectOn401` path, the URL-driven portfolio filter and single-key preference writes; the backend suites mock `PositionRepository`, `AccountService`, `SecurityApi` and `MarketPricesApi` and pin user isolation, pagination, the basis/cash/pricing semantics and per-account stamping.

The `/holdings` read path is split into phases: the SSR load returns only `holdings_table_config`, `group_mode`, `elliott_waves`, `portfolios`, `accounts`, `portfolio_id` and `account_id` (and a test asserts `getUserHoldings` is never called from the load), the browser-only effects then drive `HoldingsService.load()` to page every position and batch-load valuations and `loadAccountTotals` to fetch one `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` per uncached filtered account, and user interactions afterwards issue single-key `PATCH /accounts/me/preferences` writes or a `goto(..., { replaceState: true })` URL update for the filter — so the shell paints skeletons before any holdings request and the page survives a failed load with an in-page `holdings-error` alert.

The cost-versus-cash-flow P&L choice is made once in `PositionService._account_performance` and shared by both account-scoped totals paths: `_calculate_holding` produces per-position cost-basis P/L (`value − quantity × average_cost`), and `_account_performance` returns that positions-level P/L when `account.net_deposits` is unset but overwrites it with `value − Money(net_deposits, account.currency)` (and `return_percent` over `net_deposits` when non-zero) as soon as `net_deposits` is set — so `get_total_for_account` and `get_account_holdings` agree, deposits and withdrawals move both the dashboard badge and the account header without any position changing, and the `/holdings` header reports the same basis through the per-account totals it buckets.

`HoldingsService` models the `/holdings` filter as a discriminated `HoldingsFilter` union (`all` | `portfolio` with `portfolioId` and `accountIds` | `account` with `accountId`) with `filterByPortfolio` / `filterByAccount` / `clearFilter` setters, and its `rows` getter narrows `allRows` by an `account_id` membership test. The page mirrors the selection by calling `goto('/holdings?portfolio_id=…' | '/holdings?account_id=…', { replaceState: true })` (and `goto('/holdings')` to clear), so the URL is the source of truth for the load's filter parameters and no holdings request is made on a filter change; the same filter variant feeds the derived `filteredAccounts` that selects which accounts' server totals the header buckets, and when the filter yields nothing while `allRows` is non-empty the page shows a filter-specific empty message.

`_calculate_holding` reports the same position in three currencies: `unconverted_total_value` and `unconverted_profit_loss` in the position currency (`position.currency or security.currency`), `total_value` and `profit_loss` converted into the account currency with P/L computed as `value − quantity × average_cost`, and `display_total_value` converted on into `display_currency` (defaulting to the account currency); it also returns `converted_average_cost`/`converted_latest_price` in the account currency and the raw `latest_price`/`price_date` in the security currency.

`PositionService._account_performance` is the single basis decision behind every account-scoped total: it converts `free_cash` into the target currency and adds it to both `value` and `cost`, selects `basis = 'net_deposits'` (P/L = `value − net_deposits`, percent over `net_deposits` when non-zero) whenever `account.net_deposits` is set and otherwise `basis = 'cost'` (P/L = `positions_value − positions_cost`, percent over `positions_cost` when non-zero, with cash deliberately excluded from the denominator), and sets `pricing_incomplete = unpriced_positions > 0`.

A position whose security resolves but has no stored price is still returned as a row by `_unpriced_holding` (`total_value=0.0`, `profit_loss=None`, `converted_latest_price=None`, converted average cost preserved) while being excluded from `total_value`/`total_cost`, and it increments `unpriced_positions` — so a missing price is visible per row and reported through `pricing_incomplete` instead of silently valuing the position at zero.

`HoldingsService.loadAccountTotals(accountIds, token)` deduplicates ids with a `SvelteSet`, skips accounts already cached in `accountTotals`, returns `null` without a request when nothing is missing, fetches the rest in parallel under `Promise.allSettled` through `AccountClient.getAccountTotals(id, token)` (no `currency` parameter, so the backend defaults to each account's own currency), caches fulfilled totals by account id, and stores the first rejection's message in `errorMessage` while keeping the successful accounts.

The holdings routers resolve the display currency server-side from the user's `display_currency` preference through `UserApi.get_display_currency` (defaulting to `CAD`) and pass it into `get_user_holdings` and `get_holdings_by_security`, so `display_total_value` on every returned row is already in the user's chosen currency; `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` instead accepts an optional `?currency=` parameter validated against `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` (422 for anything else) that defaults to the account's own currency.

The `/holdings` header follows the filter: `filteredAccounts` maps the `all` variant to every loaded account, `portfolio` to the portfolio's member accounts and `account` to the single account, and a dedicated `$effect` calls `service.loadAccountTotals` for their ids inside `untrack` so the service's cache writes never become effect dependencies and only uncached accounts are requested.

The holdings table's canonical column set is nine columns (`security_symbol`, `account_name` labelled Allocation, `quantity`, `latest_price`, `total_value`, `profit_loss`, `ew_primary_target`, `ew_cycle_target`, `valuation_range`); per-row shares are computed from `display_total_value` (percent of the displayed portfolio total and per-account badge percentages), account badges are clickable and call back into the page's account filter, and the Valuation Range column opens `valuation-modal.svelte` with `onValuationChange` writing the saved valuation back into `service.valuations`.

The `/holdings` page passes raw `service.rows` plus a `groupBy` prop to the table, and `holdings-table.svelte` runs `groupHoldings(holdings, 'stock')` itself in its `baseRows` derivation; `HoldingsService.groupedHoldings` performs the same derivation over `this.rows` but is not consumed by any route, so grouping work is currently duplicated between the service and the table.

`AccountsListItemState.totals` returns a never-settling promise when `!browser`, so the accounts dashboard renders its totals skeleton during SSR and only issues `GET /accounts/{id}/totals` in the browser, and the derived promise is re-evaluated when `invalidateCache` bumps its version counter.
